global: {fief} was mine until last week, and now {player} wears its banner. The council will hear every detail of how that happened.
Congratulations to {player} on taking {fief}. I trust the garrison will be paid from your own purse this time.
Walls change hands. Loyalties change faster. I merely note that {fief} has changed masters twice since spring.
A motion to review how {fief} was lost is being drafted. Those with nothing to hide should not fear it.
{player} took {fief} while its former steward was busy keeping this council honest. Convenient timing, wouldn't you say?
I will not gloat over {fief}. I will simply keep a ledger, and the ledger is long.
whisper: {player}, enjoy {fief} while the walls still stand. Fiefs are lent here, not given, and I keep the records.
You took {fief} from a table where I still had a chair. I am patient. Patience is how councils are won.
A small piece of advice: a captured town is a debt, not a trophy. Ask whoever held it before you how that went.
I could have made {fief} very uncomfortable for you. Instead I am choosing to be generous, which you may later regret.
Do not mistake a banner for a seat on the council, {player}. Votes are counted in rooms, not on walls.
Keep {fief} if you can hold it. The next vote on fief grants will be interesting, and I intend to attend.

global: {fief} has changed hands. Such things happen. The council will decide whether the transfer was lawful.
Some fiefs are won on the field, others at the negotiating table. I have no opinion on which {player} chose.
Was {fief} lost to strategy or to luck? Those who were there will tell the council, and I will listen carefully.
I have seen {fief} change banners before. The stones remain, and so does the paperwork.
Fiefs pass from hand to hand, and so do the grudges that come with them. We shall see which lasts longer here.
The council will hold its ordinary session on {fief}'s status. Attendance is expected, and so is patience.
whisper: {player}, no hard feelings about {fief}. Politics is politics, and today the scales tipped your way.
If you intend to keep {fief}, I suggest you speak to the council before someone else does it for you.
I am not angry about {fief}. I am taking notes, which is a habit I recommend to anyone new to our council.
We may have use for each other again, {player}. Holding a fief is expensive, and I know a few ways to share costs.
The garrison at {fief} is yours now, so I assume the upkeep is too. Do let me know if you need introductions.
Enjoy the view from {fief}'s walls. Views change quickly in this realm, as I am sure you have noticed.
